prefs_lead: Personal choices, kept in your JGates data folder. They change neither the project nor what is approved.
prefs_theme_note: System follows the theme of your operating system.
prefs_language_note: The language applies to the interface text and to the messages of the local server. Changing it reloads the page.
prefs_concurrency_what: A check that only reads the synchronized copy of your project (it runs no project code, writes nothing next to the sources and starts no service) may run beside others. Every other check runs alone.
prefs_concurrency_automatic: Now: {value, plural, one {# check at a time} other {# checks at the same time}}, chosen automatically.
prefs_concurrency_configured: Now: {value, plural, one {# check at a time} other {# checks at the same time}}, as set in the configuration. Automatic would be {automatic}.
prefs_concurrency_how: Automatic means: the memory and the CPUs of the engine divided by the limits of one check ({memory} MB and {cpus} CPUs by default), never above {max}. A check stopped by the memory limit is reported as that, with a hint to lower the number.
prefs_concurrency_same: The number never changes the result: same findings, same order of checks, same decision. Cancelling stops every running check.
prefs_concurrency_link: Set the number in Configuration > Execution
prefs_more: What is not a personal preference
prefs_network_note: Network access is a run policy of the repository: it is edited in Configuration and shows up in the plan review. Run retention belongs to your data folder and lives in Storage.
prefs_providers_note: They moved to the Semantic (AI) area. That is where the defaults for every project (API keys, default models, connections) and each project's provider choice live.
